content.json:
# CAMS Executive Usage Overview

Consolidated stakeholder view of growth, engagement, feature adoption, and reliability. Built entirely from existing Application Insights telemetry (pageViews, customEvents) plus the `CAMS Sign-In` event the API records each time someone signs in.

**Known approximations:** the Growth & Engagement visuals count distinct people (by work email) from the date person-based counting started; the feature-adoption visuals still count browsers (anonymous `user_Id`), so one person on two computers counts twice there; Case Notes usage is a tab-visit proxy, not confirmed note creation; Data Verification cannot be broken out by order type (Transfer/Consolidation/Trustee Mismatch) since all three share one URL.

parameters.name: PeopleCountedFrom
parameters.query:
let activity = app('{NodeApiAppInsights:name}').customEvents
    | where name == "CAMS Sign-In"
    | project timestamp, who = tostring(customDimensions.email);
activity
| summarize firstSignIn = min(timestamp)
| project CountedFrom = iff(isnull(firstSignIn),
    "No sign-ins have been recorded yet, so person-based counts are empty.",
    strcat("People counted from ", format_datetime(firstSignIn, "yyyy-MM-dd"), "."))

parameters.name: PeopleRangeNote
PeopleCohortNote

content.json:
## Growth & Engagement

**{PeopleCountedFrom}** Every chart in this section counts distinct people, identified by the work email recorded when they sign in, so one person on two computers counts once. Person-based numbers start on that date and are not back-filled; earlier periods are only in *Browser-based history* at the end of this section. Dates are UTC.

**Growth Summary** gives three top-line numbers for the selected time range: how many distinct people signed in, how many signed in for the first time, and the change in active people compared with the immediately preceding period of the same length (e.g. if you're viewing the last 7 days, this compares against the 7 days before that). Growth % is shown only when person-based counting covers the whole prior period. New People is overstated for ranges starting within 30 days of the date counting started, because people who used CAMS before that date look new. Sign-ins with no work email are not counted; when there are any in the range, the Active People tile says how many.

content.title: Growth Summary (people)

content.json: **DAU / WAU / MAU** count distinct people who signed in per day, over a rolling 7-day window, and over a rolling 30-day window, for each day of the selected range from the date counting started. **Stickiness** (DAU÷MAU) is a standard engagement measure — the higher it is, the more the monthly total is made up of people who show up daily rather than just once a month. For the first 30 days after counting started, WAU and MAU only include days since that date, so MAU reads low and Stickiness reads high. The last day shown is usually today, still in progress, so its DAU and Stickiness read low.

content.title: DAU / WAU / MAU and Stickiness (DAU÷MAU %) — people
content.noDataMessage: No sign-ins in the selected time range.

content.json: **Engaged vs. Occasional People** splits the people who signed in during the selected range by how many distinct days they signed in: 8 or more days is "Engaged", 1 to 7 is "Occasional" (the 8-day line is provisional). **New vs. Returning People** splits the same people by whether their first recorded sign-in falls inside the range ("New") or earlier ("Returning").

**These two charts read high for now.** Person-based counting started less than 30 days before the start of the selected range. People who used CAMS before counting started show as New the first time they sign in after it, and only their days since then count toward Engaged, so New reads high and Engaged reads low. This note goes away once the range starts 30 or more days after counting started.

content.query:
let activity = app('{NodeApiAppInsights:name}').customEvents
    | where name == "CAMS Sign-In"
    | project timestamp, who = tostring(customDimensions.email);
let RangeStart = {TimeRange:start};
let RangeEnd = {TimeRange:end};
activity
| where isnotempty(who)
| where timestamp >= RangeStart and timestamp < RangeEnd
| distinct who, Day = startofday(timestamp)
| summarize ActiveDays = count() by who
| extend Segment = iff(ActiveDays >= 8, "Engaged (8+ active days)", "Occasional (1-7 active days)")
| summarize People = count() by Segment
| order by Segment asc
content.title: Engaged vs. Occasional People
content.noDataMessage: No sign-ins in the selected time range.

content.title: New vs. Returning People
content.noDataMessage: No sign-ins in the selected time range.

content.json: **Weekly Cohort Retention** groups people by the week of their first recorded sign-in (their "cohort"), then shows what percentage of each cohort signed in again in each later week, up to week 8. Week 0 is always 100%. Each line is one starting week; a line that drops fast means those people didn't keep using CAMS. Cohorts from the last 70 days are shown, whatever time range is selected. Weeks start on Sunday (UTC).

**This chart reads high for now.** The earliest cohort shown starts less than 30 days after person-based counting started. People who used CAMS before then join a cohort in the week they first sign in after that date, so early cohorts include long-time users and retain better than genuinely new people. This note goes away once the earliest cohort shown starts 30 or more days after counting started, about 100 days after it started.

content.query:
let activity = app('{NodeApiAppInsights:name}').customEvents
    | where name == "CAMS Sign-In"
    | project timestamp, who = tostring(customDimensions.email);
let ids = activity | where isnotempty(who);
let cohorts = ids
    | summarize CohortWeek = startofweek(min(timestamp)) by who
    | where CohortWeek > now() - 70d;
let cohortSizes = cohorts | summarize CohortSize = count() by CohortWeek;
ids
| where timestamp > now() - 77d
| distinct who, ActiveWeek = startofweek(timestamp)
| join kind=inner cohorts on who
| extend WeekNumber = datetime_diff('week', ActiveWeek, CohortWeek)
| where WeekNumber between (0 .. 8)
| summarize Active = count() by CohortWeek, WeekNumber
| join kind=inner cohortSizes on CohortWeek
| project CohortWeek = format_datetime(CohortWeek, "yyyy-MM-dd"), WeekNumber,
    RetentionPercent = round(100.0 * Active / CohortSize, 1)
| order by CohortWeek asc, WeekNumber asc
content.title: Weekly Cohort Retention (% of cohort still signing in by week N) — people
content.noDataMessage: No sign-ins in the last 70 days.

content.json: These are the original browser-based counts, kept for comparison and for periods before person-based counting started. Each browser (App Insights' anonymous `user_Id`) counts separately, so one person on two computers counts twice.

**Growth Summary** gives three top-line numbers for the selected time range: how many distinct browsers were active, how many showed up for the first time, and how that compares to the immediately preceding period of the same length (e.g. if you're viewing the last 7 days, this compares against the 7 days before that). Growth % is shown only when the oldest telemetry still kept covers the whole prior period, and New Users is overstated for ranges starting within 30 days of that oldest telemetry.

content.title: Growth Summary (browsers)

content.json: **DAU / WAU / MAU** count distinct active browsers per day, over a rolling 7-day window, and over a rolling 30-day window. **Stickiness** (DAU÷MAU) is a standard engagement measure — the higher it is, the more the monthly total is made up of people who show up daily rather than just once a month. Days within 30 days of the oldest telemetry still kept have partial WAU and MAU windows, so MAU reads low. The last day shown is usually today, still in progress, so its DAU and Stickiness read low.

content.title: DAU / WAU / MAU and Stickiness (DAU÷MAU %) — browsers

content.json: **Engaged vs. Occasional Users** splits browsers by how many distinct days they were active in the period: 8+ days is "Engaged," fewer is "Occasional" (that 8-day line is provisional — see the open ticket item to tune it against real traffic). **New vs. Returning Users** splits browsers by whether their very first-ever visit falls inside the selected period ("New") or happened earlier ("Returning"). New Users is overstated for ranges starting within 30 days of the oldest telemetry still kept.

content.query:
union pageViews, customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| summarize ActiveDays = dcount(startofday(timestamp)) by user_Id
| extend Segment = iif(ActiveDays >= 8, "Engaged (8+ active days)", "Occasional (1-7 active days)")
| summarize Users = count() by Segment
content.title: Engaged vs. Occasional Users (browsers)
New vs. Returning Users (browsers)

content.json: **Weekly Cohort Retention** groups users by the week they first showed up (their "cohort"), then tracks what percentage of that same group is still active in each week afterward. Each line is one starting week; a line that drops fast means those users didn't stick around, a line that stays high means they kept coming back. Because it takes a few weeks to build up a retention curve, only cohorts old enough to have that history are shown. Cohorts starting within 30 days of the oldest telemetry still kept include returning browsers, so they read high.

content.query:
let activity = union pageViews, customEvents
    | project timestamp, who = user_Id;
let ids = activity | where isnotempty(who);
let cohorts = ids
    | summarize CohortWeek = startofweek(min(timestamp)) by who
    | where CohortWeek > now() - 70d;
let cohortSizes = cohorts | summarize CohortSize = count() by CohortWeek;
ids
| where timestamp > now() - 77d
| distinct who, ActiveWeek = startofweek(timestamp)
| join kind=inner cohorts on who
| extend WeekNumber = datetime_diff('week', ActiveWeek, CohortWeek)
| where WeekNumber between (0 .. 8)
| summarize Active = count() by CohortWeek, WeekNumber
| join kind=inner cohortSizes on CohortWeek
| project CohortWeek = format_datetime(CohortWeek, "yyyy-MM-dd"), WeekNumber,
    RetentionPercent = round(100.0 * Active / CohortSize, 1)
| order by CohortWeek asc, WeekNumber asc
content.title: Weekly Cohort Retention (% of cohort still active by week N) — browsers

content.json:
## Feature Adoption

Every case-detail and trustee-detail tab is a distinct route, and the app already auto-tracks a `pageView` on every route change — so this is a direct measure of which tabs are actually being visited, no new instrumentation needed. **Data Verification** is a single URL (its three order types render as accordions, not routes) so it cannot be broken out further without new instrumentation.
**Tab-Level Adoption** ranks every tab and section by what percentage of all active users visited it at least once during the period — a snapshot of which features get used at all.

content.query:
let Routes = pageViews
    | where timestamp {TimeRange}
    | where isnotempty(url)
    | extend Section = case(
        url contains "/case-detail/" or url contains "/my-cases" or (url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/")), "Cases",
        url contains "/trustees", "Trustees",
        url contains "/data-verification", "Data Verification",
        url contains "/staff-assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | extend Tab = case(
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/my-cases", "My Cases (list)",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/"), "Case Search",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee-and-assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/court-docket", "Court Docket",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/notes", "Case Notes",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/associated-cases", "Associated Cases",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee", "Trustee",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/case-detail/", "Overview",
        Section == "Trustees" and url endswith "/trustees", "Trustees List",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/appointments", "Appointments",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/notes", "Trustee Notes",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/cases", "Case List",
        Section == "Trustees", "Overview",
        Section == "Data Verification", "Data Verification",
        Section == "Staff Assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | where Section != "Other";
let TotalActiveUsers = toscalar(pageViews | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize dcount(user_Id));
Routes
| summarize UsersVisiting = dcount(user_Id) by Section, Tab
| extend ['% of Active Users'] = round(100.0 * UsersVisiting / TotalActiveUsers, 1)
| project Section, Tab, UsersVisiting, ['% of Active Users']
| order by Section asc, ['% of Active Users'] desc
content.title: Tab-Level Adoption (% of active users visiting each tab)

content.json: **Tab Adoption Trend** shows that same tab-visit metric broken out week by week instead of as one snapshot, so you can see whether adoption of a tab (or a whole section, via the filter below) is growing, flat, or shrinking over time.

content.query:
let Routes = pageViews
    | where timestamp {TimeRange}
    | where isnotempty(url)
    | extend Section = case(
        url contains "/case-detail/" or url contains "/my-cases" or (url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/")), "Cases",
        url contains "/trustees", "Trustees",
        url contains "/data-verification", "Data Verification",
        url contains "/staff-assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | extend Tab = case(
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/my-cases", "My Cases (list)",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/"), "Case Search",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee-and-assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/court-docket", "Court Docket",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/notes", "Case Notes",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/associated-cases", "Associated Cases",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee", "Trustee",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/case-detail/", "Overview",
        Section == "Trustees" and url endswith "/trustees", "Trustees List",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/appointments", "Appointments",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/notes", "Trustee Notes",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/cases", "Case List",
        Section == "Trustees", "Overview",
        Section == "Data Verification", "Data Verification",
        Section == "Staff Assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | where Section != "Other";
let TotalActiveUsers = toscalar(pageViews | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize dcount(user_Id));
Routes
| where '{SectionFilter}' == 'value::all' or Section == '{SectionFilter}'
| summarize UsersVisiting = dcount(user_Id) by Tab, Week = startofweek(timestamp)
| extend ['% of Active Users'] = round(100.0 * UsersVisiting / TotalActiveUsers, 1)
| order by Week asc
content.title: Tab Adoption Trend

content.json: **Search Click-Through Rate** approximates search success: of all searches performed, what percentage were followed by a click on a result within 5 minutes. There's no "zero results" signal in telemetry today, so this is the closest available proxy — a low rate could mean bad results, or just a user who found what they needed some other way.

content.query:
let SearchEvents = customEvents | where timestamp {TimeRange} | where name == "search" | project session_Id, SearchTime = timestamp;
let ClickEvents = customEvents | where timestamp {TimeRange} | where name == "searchResultClick" | project session_Id, ClickTime = timestamp;
SearchEvents
| join kind=leftouter ClickEvents on session_Id
| where isnull(ClickTime) or ClickTime >= SearchTime
| summarize HadClick = max(isnotempty(ClickTime) and (ClickTime - SearchTime) < 5m) by session_Id, SearchTime
| summarize TotalSearches = count(), SearchesWithClick = countif(HadClick)
| extend ['Click-Through Rate %'] = round(iif(TotalSearches > 0, 100.0 * SearchesWithClick / TotalSearches, 0.0), 1)
| project TotalSearches, SearchesWithClick, ['Click-Through Rate %']
content.title: Search Click-Through Rate (proxy for search success — no zero-result field exists in telemetry today)

content.json:
### Notes Engagement

Called out specifically since stakeholders have asked about these two features. **Trustee Notes Engagement** is pulled directly from the existing nightly Trustee Notes aggregate: what percentage of trustees have at least one note, what percentage of users have engaged with notes, and how many notes were created in the last 24 hours. **Case Notes Visit Rate** is a rougher proxy — no equivalent backend aggregate exists yet for Case Notes, so this only measures what percentage of users who opened a case detail page also clicked into its Notes tab, not whether they actually wrote anything.

content.query:
app('{DataflowsAppInsights:name}').customEvents
| where customDimensions.moduleName == "SYNC-TRUSTEE-NOTES-METRICS"
| where name == "DataflowHandlerComplete"
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| extend
    TrusteesWithNotesPercent = todouble(customDimensions.trusteesWithNotesPercent),
    UserEngagementPercent = todouble(customDimensions.userEngagementPercent),
    NotesLast24Hrs = todouble(customDimensions.notesLast24Hrs)
| summarize
    ['Trustees With Notes %'] = round(max(TrusteesWithNotesPercent), 1),
    ['User Engagement %'] = round(max(UserEngagementPercent), 1),
    ['Notes Created (last 24h)'] = round(max(NotesLast24Hrs), 0)
    by Day = startofday(timestamp)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Trustee Notes Engagement (from existing SYNC-TRUSTEE-NOTES-METRICS aggregate)
Case Notes Visit Rate (proxy — tab visits, not confirmed note creation; no backend aggregate exists yet)

content.json:
## Reliability & Data Quality

System health, framed as the trust signal behind the usage numbers above.

**Page Load** and **Search Latency** show the P50 (typical) and P95 (worst-case-for-most-users) response times in milliseconds, day by day — a proxy for whether the app feels fast or sluggish to users.

content.query:
pageViews
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| summarize P50Ms = percentile(duration, 50), P95Ms = percentile(duration, 95) by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Page Load Latency (P50 / P95, ms)

content.query:
customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where name == "Case Search Performance"
| extend DurationMs = todouble(customMeasurements.durationMs)
| summarize P50Ms = percentile(DurationMs, 50), P95Ms = percentile(DurationMs, 95) by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Search Latency (P50 / P95, ms)

content.json: **Frontend Exception Rate** normalizes JavaScript errors against traffic volume (errors per 1,000 page views) so a spike isn't just an artifact of more people using the app. **Dataflow Sync Success Rate** tracks the health of the backend jobs that keep CAMS data in sync — a drop here means the numbers elsewhere in this workbook (and in the app itself) may be stale.

content.query:
let dailyExceptions = exceptions | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize Exceptions = count() by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d);
let dailyViews = pageViews | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize Views = count() by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d);
dailyViews
| join kind=fullouter dailyExceptions on Day
| project Day = coalesce(Day, Day1), Exceptions = coalesce(Exceptions, 0), Views = coalesce(Views, 0)
| extend ['Exceptions per 1,000 Views'] = round(iif(Views > 0, 1000.0 * Exceptions / Views, 0.0), 2)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Frontend Exception Rate

content.query:
app('{DataflowsAppInsights:name}').customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where name == "DataflowHandlerComplete"
| extend Success = tostring(customDimensions.success)
| summarize Total = count(), Succeeded = countif(Success == "true") by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| extend ['Success Rate %'] = round(iif(Total > 0, 100.0 * Succeeded / Total, 0.0), 1)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Dataflow Sync Success Rate (data freshness health)
